highlights.text: The three letters point to ذُلّ (being brought low, humbled)
the active participle دَاخِرٌ = one who is abased/humbled
afḍā ilā imraʾatihi, "he reached his wife"
"their food is fawḍā faḍan in their abodes"
core sense is bringing something about — an action (ʿamal) or otherwise
faʿaltu kadhā afʿaluhu faʿlan — "I did such-a-thing, I do it,"
a discrete deed
a single word (kalima) that indicates repugnance and aversion
A man who is faẓẓ is one of repugnant character
core sense is "something crushed/broken into fragments."
Noun al-farth: what is inside the karish (the stomach/rumen) — its contents
core idea is youthfulness together with the surging of (sexual) desire
a youth or boy — specifically one whose moustache is just beginning to sprout
One core word from which further senses are drawn by likeness/metaphor.
"every one who comes to face the water [jābih] gets one draught [jawzah]
a single root meaning (aṣl wāḥid): coming to know a thing through a light, gentle touch
because a spy finds out what he wants in secret and with subtlety
the underlying sense of the verb is kharaqtu
al-jayb is the jayb of a shirt/garment — the opening (e.g. at the neck or bosom)
The verb is used of fire "scorching" someone with its heat
a single underlying sense: the outward look or complexion of a thing (سَحْنَة)
لَوْن (lawn) is the colour of a thing — for example redness or blackness
a sound root whose sense is running off and parting
the one who takes the opposing side in a matter
"lest al-Sandarī be my rival (nadīdatī)
core idea is a thing being cut off and running out
a thing is used up, runs out, comes to an end
if you speak (contend) with them, they will speak (contend) back at you
something coming out of a mouth or opening with the faintest sound
a proverb holds that a person with an afflicted chest must expel breath
something turned away from — rejected or held undesirable
the most reduced or worst stage of a lifespan
the people a community regards as its lowest
a surplus/margin gained in a transaction
rabiḥa fulānun fī bayʿihi — so-and-so gained a profit in his sale
illustrated with a citation from al-Aʿshā
closing up a gap or breach
a noun for the resulting barrier/rampart itself
"has the [array of] poets left anything unpatched-over..."
a thing's being evenly ordered and regularly arranged in a straight line
letting the word issue from the mouth easily and straightly
a covering and a concealment
al-rayn — a covering over something
a hadith of ʿUmar about a man of Juhaynah who ran recklessly into debt and "was rīna bihi" by morning — glossed as: he died
a root (aṣl) that indicates overpowering and rising above
Saṭā ʿalayhi, yasṭū: he overpowered him with violent force.
intense anger — specifically the kind of anger that calls for punishment to follow
by its effect: the sending down of punishment
as covering two unrelated words
The second word appears in the phrase ذَرْ ذَا (dhar dhā, "leave this alone")
Al-waṭan — a person's dwelling-place, the place where one settles/resides.
decoration that has been prettified or gilded
gold itself is called zukhruf
the prettified, dressed-up parts of speech — words given an attractive surface
the beauty of something and the act of making it beautiful
is defined as the opposite of الشَّيْن
the earth became beautiful
